nevsky: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and the Icon Crypt

The great cathedral with its golden domes is the symbol of Sofia, built in memory of the soldiers who fell in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78. Inside you walk among mosaics and marble; beneath the church, in the crypt, is a collection of icons from the Middle Ages to the 19th century.
serdica: Roman Serdica, the Largo and St George Rotunda

At the very centre of Sofia, next to Serdika metro station, are the ruins of Roman Serdica, free to walk through. Around them opens the Largo, the great open space with socialist-era buildings, the church of Sveta Nedelya and, in a courtyard, the St George Rotunda, the city's oldest building.
banya: Banya Bashi Mosque, Synagogue and Central Market

Three places very close together: the 16th-century mosque built over hot springs, the great Sephardic synagogue, one of the largest in Europe, and the Central Market Hall, a restored historic building with shops, bars and small restaurants.
vitosha: Vitosha Boulevard, Ivan Vazov Theatre and City Garden

The main pedestrian street, with shops, cafés and Mount Vitosha in the background. At the end is the City Garden with the Ivan Vazov National Theatre, a neoclassical building with a pale, gilded façade, the country's oldest theatre.
archeo: The museum of Bulgaria's treasures, from the Stone Age to the Middle Ages, housed in a former great Ottoman mosque. The treasure room with Thracian gold is the best part; it's small and takes about an hour.
sofiachurch: St Sofia Basilica and the Russian Church

The red-brick St Sofia Basilica dates from the 6th century and gave the city its name; beneath the church is a small museum with ancient tombs. A few steps away, the Russian Church of St Nicholas has five golden domes on a green roof.
boyana: A small medieval church at the foot of Mount Vitosha, a UNESCO site, famous for its 1259 frescoes, among the most important works of Byzantine art in Eastern Europe. Outside is a quiet garden.
ndk: The huge 1980s concrete congress centre, a symbol of socialist Sofia, in a large park with fountains. A place to walk and look at the architecture, with Mount Vitosha in the background.
socialist: A museum and park with giant statues from Bulgaria's communist era: Lenin, workers and soldiers in bronze and stone, removed from the squares after 1989. Inside are paintings and posters.
